paper: ATLAS Professor: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of 1.58-bit Ternary LLMs
hardware: Intel Core i7-7700T (Kaby Lake, 4C/8T @ 2.9 GHz, 8 MB L3), DDR4-2400, 16 GB
engine: ATLAS TQ1.0 v2.11, hybrid int4 FFN + TQ1-packed QKV/O, AVX2

1.7B.architecture: 28L/2048H/6144I/16:8 heads/128hdim/151669vocab, Qwen3, SwiGLU, YaRN RoPE theta=1M, Tie Embeddings
1.7B.merge: full (all 7 QKV/O/gate/up/down targets), LoRA rank=16, alpha=32

4B.architecture: 36L/2560H/9728I/32:8 heads/128hdim/151669vocab, Qwen3, SwiGLU, YaRN RoPE theta=5M f4, Tie Embeddings

capital_of_france.pro_v2: fails: 'Paris... sorry, I cant tell you why' (DPO collapse)

explain_quantum.pro_v2: fails: 'uses 0s and 1s... uses 0s and 1s' (same thing twice)

key_findings: Full LoRA merge (all 7 targets) produces zero speed overhead: baseline and finetuned models show identical tok/s (4.5 for 4B, 11.1 for 1.7B)
Full merge preserves output quality: 5/5 prompts correct for both 1.7B and 4B
Attention-only merge (4B v2) causes DPO collapse on 3/5 prompts: repetitive, nonsensical, or incorrect outputs
Training signal requires all-layer application: restricting updates to attention layers creates inconsistency with unchanged FFN layers
Ternary 1.58-bit CPU inference at ~4.5 tok/s (4B) and ~11 tok/s (1.7B) is viable for interactive applications on consumer hardware (i7-7700T, 16 GB DDR4)
